question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x+4y+2z=3 \\  & y=-1 \\  & z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that the matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form.

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-4){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=5 \\  & y=-1 \\  & z=1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=5$, $y=-1$, and $z=1.$
